name: Side-lying hip abduction
summary: Lying on your side, lift the straight top leg toward the ceiling with the toes pointing forward.
setup: Lie on your side facing the phone, which sits on the floor about 2 m away. Bottom knee bent for balance, top leg straight and in line with the body. Lift the top leg 30–40° with the toes pointing ahead, pause, lower slowly.
brief: Lie on your side, bottom knee bent for balance, top leg straight and in line with the body. Lift the top leg 30 to 40 degrees with the toes pointing ahead, pause, then lower slowly.
why: The top leg swings up in the camera plane, so its angle from the body counts the reps. The leg drifting forward and the pelvis rolling back are along the phone axis and are not judged.
tempo: Up 2 s, hold 1 s, down 3 s.
progression: Ankle weight; toes turned slightly down.
regression: Smaller lift; bend the bottom knee more.
contraindications: Pain on the outside of the hip that lingers after the set.

faults.label: Not reaching the target
faults.tip: Take each rep through the full range you set — half reps count as partials.

faults.label: Too fast
faults.tip: Control both directions; momentum takes the work away from the muscle.

faults.label: Leg drifting forward
faults.tip: Lift in line with the body or a touch behind it. Forward lifting hands the work to the hip flexors.

faults.label: Rolling the trunk back
faults.tip: Keep the shoulders and hips stacked; a hand on the floor in front stops the roll.

faults.label: Toes turning to the ceiling
faults.tip: Turning the toes up swaps the glute for the hip flexor at the front of the hip.

faults.label: Lifting too high
faults.tip: Past about 45° the pelvis tips and the waist muscles take over. Lower is better here.

guide.stop: Outer hip pain that lingers, or pinching.
guide.cannotSee: The leg drifting forward, the toes turning up, the trunk rolling.

points.t: Shoulders and hips stacked; do not roll back.
